questions.q: Which level of data abstraction describes how the data is actually stored on storage devices?
questions.explanation: The physical level describes storage structures such as files, blocks and indexes. The logical level describes what data is stored and how it is related, and the view level shows only a part of the database to a user.

questions.q: The logical level of data abstraction describes:
options: How records are laid out in disk blocks
What data is stored in the database and the relationships among that data
Only the part of the database visible to one user
The access paths such as B-tree indexes
questions.explanation: The logical (conceptual) level describes the entities, attributes and relationships, i.e. WHAT is stored. HOW it is stored belongs to the physical level.

questions.q: The main purpose of the view level of abstraction is to:
options: Increase the storage capacity of the database
Reduce the number of tables in the schema
Simplify user interaction by showing only the relevant part of the database
questions.explanation: A view hides the complexity of the full database and shows each user only the data they need. This also helps security, since sensitive columns can be left out of a view.

questions.q: The overall design of a database, which changes rarely, is called the:
questions.explanation: The schema is the logical structure (tables, attributes, constraints). The instance is the actual data stored at a particular moment, which keeps changing.

questions.q: The collection of information stored in a database at a particular moment is called an:
questions.explanation: A database instance is the data in the database at a given time. Schema is the design; instance is the content, like a class versus its objects in programming.

questions.q: Physical data independence means the ability to:
options: Change the logical schema without changing the application programs
Store data on more than one computer
Change the physical schema without changing the logical schema
Hide the database from the network
questions.explanation: With physical data independence we can change storage details (a new index, a different file organisation, a new disk) without rewriting the logical schema or the applications.

questions.q: Logical data independence is the ability to change the:
options: Physical storage device without any restart
Operating system without changing the DBMS
Conceptual schema without changing the external schemas or application programs
questions.explanation: Logical data independence lets us modify the conceptual schema (for example, add a new attribute) without forcing changes in user views or application programs.

questions.q: Which type of data independence is harder to achieve?
options: Neither can be achieved in any DBMS
questions.explanation: Application programs depend directly on the logical structure (tables and attributes), so logical changes often affect them. Physical changes are easily hidden by the mapping between the logical and physical levels.

questions.q: Data independence is achieved in a DBMS mainly through:
options: Mappings between the levels of the three-schema architecture
Allowing only one user at a time
questions.explanation: The DBMS keeps mappings between the external, conceptual and internal schemas. When one level changes, only the mapping is updated and the levels above stay unchanged.

questions.q: Data Definition Language (DDL) is used to:
options: Define and modify the database schema
questions.explanation: DDL defines the structure of the database: creating, altering and dropping tables, indexes and constraints. Working with the data inside the tables is done with DML.

questions.q: Which of the following is a DDL command?
questions.explanation: ALTER changes the structure of an existing table, so it is DDL. SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE work on the data and are DML.

questions.q: The output of DDL statements is stored in the:
questions.explanation: DDL statements produce metadata (table names, columns, constraints) which the DBMS stores in the data dictionary, also called the system catalog.

questions.q: Data Manipulation Language (DML) is used to:
options: Access, insert, delete and modify the data stored in the database
Define integrity constraints on the schema
questions.explanation: DML works on the data itself: retrieving, inserting, deleting and modifying rows. Creating tables and constraints is DDL, and granting privileges is DCL.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a DML command?
questions.explanation: CREATE defines a new database object, so it is DDL. SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE are used to read or change data, so they are DML.

questions.q: A declarative (non-procedural) DML, such as SQL, requires the user to specify:
options: How to fetch the data, step by step
The exact disk blocks to read
The order in which indexes are searched
What data is needed, without specifying how to get it
questions.explanation: In a declarative language you state WHAT you want and the DBMS query optimizer decides HOW to get it. A procedural DML requires the programmer to give the steps.

questions.q: The TRUNCATE command is classified as:
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE removes all rows of a table at once and is treated as a DDL command (in Oracle it commits automatically). DELETE, which removes selected rows, is DML.

questions.q: In a three-tier DBMS architecture, the correct order of tiers from the user to the data is:
questions.explanation: The user works in the presentation tier (client), which talks to the application tier containing the business logic, and only that tier talks to the database tier.

questions.q: In a two-tier architecture, the client application communicates:
questions.explanation: Two-tier means client and database server only. The client sends SQL directly to the server (for example through ODBC or JDBC). Three-tier adds an application server in between.

questions.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of a Database Administrator (DBA)?
options: Defining storage structure, granting access authorisation and managing backup and recovery
Designing the graphical interface of applications
questions.explanation: The DBA looks after the database as a whole: schema definition, storage structure and access methods, user authorisation, performance tuning, and backup and recovery.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of a DBMS over a traditional file-processing system?
options: Programs depend on the file format
Data is isolated in separate files
questions.explanation: A DBMS keeps data in one central place, so the same fact is not stored many times. This lowers redundancy and inconsistency. The other options are drawbacks of file systems.

questions.q: Which of the following is a record-based logical data model?
questions.explanation: Record-based models store data in fixed-format records. The relational, network and hierarchical models are record-based. The ER, object-oriented and semantic models are object-based.

questions.q: The entity-relationship (ER) model was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Peter Chen proposed the ER model in 1976. E. F. Codd proposed the relational model and Charles Bachman is associated with the network model.

questions.q: In an ER diagram, an entity set is represented by a:
questions.explanation: Rectangle = entity set, ellipse = attribute, diamond = relationship set, and lines connect them.

questions.q: A multivalued attribute (for example, phone numbers of a person) is shown in an ER diagram by a:
questions.explanation: A double ellipse marks a multivalued attribute. A dashed ellipse is a derived attribute and an underlined name marks a key attribute.

questions.q: A derived attribute (for example, age derived from date of birth) is shown by a:
questions.explanation: A derived attribute can be computed from other attributes, so it is drawn with a dashed ellipse. Age can always be calculated from date of birth.
